Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller piece of that same problem. Each call does a little work, then hands the rest off to another call of itself, kind of like a line of people each passing a bucket until only one scoop remains. To keep this from going on forever, you always need a base case — a simple condition where the function just returns an answer directly instead of calling itself again. A classic example is factorial: `factorial(n)` returns `n * factorial(n - 1)`, until it hits `factorial(1)`, which simply returns `1` and stops the chain.
